clues: This small city sits on a big river near the geographic center of its state. Across the river lies another state.
Summers here are hot and humid, with more than 20 days a year topping 90 degrees. Rain falls fairly evenly through the year.
On November 25, 1790, this town took the state capital job. A few years prior, it had been the capital of the whole young land.
On the night of Christmas in 1776, George Washington crossed the icy river by boat. His men then beat the foe troops in this town.
The governor of New Jersey works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, a short walk from the river.
